title: I started building a news app in my bedroom because I couldn't find a way to stay informed without feeling overwhelmed.
body:
The problem wasn't a lack of information. It was the noise. Every morning, I was bombarded with hundreds of headlines, most of which had nothing to do with what I actually cared about or needed to know. I wanted to understand the world, but the current systems were designed to keep me clicking, not to keep me informed.

That frustration led me to build Headlinne. I wanted to see if AI could act as a filter instead of a megaphone. Instead of showing everyone the same sensational stories, we built a system that learns what matters to you personally. It does not guess. It learns from what you actually read and value.

Building this as a teenager taught me that technology is only useful when it solves a real human problem. We are not trying to replace journalism. We are trying to make it accessible again. We want to give people their time back by cutting through the clutter so they can focus on the stories that shape their world.
cta: You can see how we are rethinking the news experience at HEADLINNE.com.
